claims.text: The sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates are uncoated metal parts directly exposed to high-temperature molten aluminum.
Applying a high-purity alumina ceramic coating will reduce molten-aluminum corrosion relative to uncoated metal parts.
The ceramic coating forms an inert alumina layer.
The alumina layer resists penetration by liquid aluminum.
The alumina coating acts as a passive barrier between molten aluminum and the underlying metal.
Limiting direct contact between molten aluminum and the underlying metal minimizes corrosive reactions and material degradation.
Alumina-coated parts will exhibit significantly lower corrosion depths than uncoated parts after the same exposure duration.
Alumina-coated parts will exhibit significantly lower weight loss than uncoated parts after the same exposure duration.
Alumina-coated parts will retain greater mechanical integrity than uncoated parts after the same exposure duration.
Uncoated metal parts typically suffer considerable corrosion and erosion in high-temperature molten aluminum.
Poor coating adhesion during thermal cycling may limit the coating's protective effect.
Microcracking may limit the coating's protective effect.
Operating near the alumina coating's stability limit may reduce its protective effect.
Repeated thermal and mechanical stress may compromise the long-term durability of the alumina coating.
Variation in coating application quality may affect protective performance.
